solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Capacity of crew seeing across delta

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, so one piece spans another

blocks.note: a band is a group or gang of people
if you are seeing someone you are going out with them
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sailor's crew, out on the water, can see right across a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' is the dating sense, as in going out with someone, not using your eyes; 'delta' is a radio-alphabet letter rather than a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandwidth is the data-carrying capacity of a network link, and loosely anyone's spare mental capacity.

clue.text: Hide family money first

indicators.note: first tells us which of the two pieces is placed at the front

blocks.note: bucks are dollars, informal money
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone hides the family fortune before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb about stashing cash, but it is the noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckskin is leather made from the skin of a deer, a hide in the tanning sense.

clue.text: Location of bridge over one sound

indicators.note: something laid over another covers it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the bridge of the nose is the bony ridge at its top
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Directions to a bridge spanning a sound, a stretch of sea between islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is not over water: it is the one on your face. 'Sound' looks like a body of water but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, particularly a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Don’t show supporting members what union leader will do

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: cover up your legs, the limbs that hold you up
second meaning: the idiom for being the dominant partner in a marriage

explanation.surface: Sounds like a trade union boss refusing to show supportive members of the union.
explanation.walkthrough: The union is a marriage, not a trade union, and the supporting members are legs, not union members.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the partner who makes the decisions in a household; literally, trousers hide the legs.

clue.text: Poor harmony is leading issue in disco music

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so one piece is placed ahead of the next
in places the preceding letters inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
a son is a child, one's issue
dance is a genre of club and disco music

explanation.surface: Out-of-tune harmony is the main problem with disco tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading issue' looks like 'main problem', but issue is offspring and leading just puts IS in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissonance is a clash of notes that do not sit well together, the opposite of good harmony.

clue.text: Drinking a Tango he can’t stand

indicators.note: someone drinking takes liquid inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man drinking a Tango, an orange fizzy drink sold in Britain, that he dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British soft drink in the surface, but the setter uses it for its radio-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to be unable to bear or tolerate it.

clue.text: Mendicant king with fine clothing

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so one piece dresses another

blocks.note: fine weather is fair weather
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A beggar king dressed in fine clothes, a fairy-tale reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' reads as a noun for garments but works as a verb: the fine word clothes the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu holy man who lives by begging, and mendicant means beggar.

clue.text: Fancy version of team-building

blocks.note: surface reading: an elaborate corporate away-day exercise
setter's reading: picking an imaginary squad of real players, an imagined take on the sport

explanation.walkthrough: Fancy looks like an adjective for posh, but it means imagination; team-building is literal selecting of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: In this online game you assemble a squad of real players and score points from their real matches, an imagined pastime.

clue.text: Rise to embrace comedian, a wise guy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece holds others in its arms

blocks.note: a knoll is a small hill, a rise in the ground
a wit is a clever, funny person
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stands to hug a comedian who is a bit of a smart alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a verb but is the noun for a hillock.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a smart alec who acts as if they have every answer, the same sort of person.

clue.text: Spoke right before a call

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces in front of the later one

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
to dial is to telephone, to call someone

explanation.surface: Someone talked just ahead of making a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past tense of speak, but it is the noun for a wheel's rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a line or bar running out from a centre, as a wheel's rods do from the hub.

clue.text: Potentially one’s best friend

blocks.note: first meaning: the good porcelain, 'the best' brought out for guests, and a product of the potter
second meaning: rhyming slang

explanation.surface: Someone who could turn out to be your best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' hides POT, pointing to pottery: the best dinner service is called 'the best china'. In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain tableware is kept as the household's best set, and in London slang a mate is a china.

clue.text: Can seek to cut down tree

indicators.note: to here means going into, so the first pair of pieces is put inside the next

blocks.note: a tin is a can
to woo is to seek someone's favour or hand
someone cut down is deflated and sad

explanation.surface: A lumberjack asks whether he can try to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' looks like felling the tree, but it means dejected; 'Can' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a tropical tree prized for its glossy, smooth timber.

clue.text: Poles returned to gather tiny fruit

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards
to gather is to take in and hold, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: posts are poles
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Polish people go back home to pick small fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' tempts as Polish people or as the N and S compass letters, but it means posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetsop, or sugar apple, is a tropical fruit with sweet custardy pulp.

clue.text: Dad keeps ignoring Mr Martin Sheen

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
to ignore is to leave out, so some letters are dropped

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the first name, taken as written
the title, whose letters are removed from the name

explanation.surface: A father carries on overlooking the actor Martin Sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Sheen looks like one name, but Sheen is the definition and only 'Martin' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is the gloss or film that forms on old wood, bronze or leather with age.

clue.text: Fagin’s cronies finally go to court?

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: Bill Sikes and company, Fagin's gang in Oliver Twist
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fagin's criminal gang at last faces trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist; Co is short for company. Court is the romantic verb, not a lawcourt.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill and coo is to kiss and murmur lovingly, like doves, which is how lovers court.

clue.text: Pregnant a year after life with many changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered and rearranged
after puts the first pieces behind the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Expecting a baby a year on, a life with lots of upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many changes' looks like one phrase, but 'many' is fodder and only 'changes' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The old euphemism describes a woman expecting a child.

clue.text: Try to accept everyone’s for romance?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece receives others inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
everyone is all, plus the 's
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitor is urged to try to welcome everyone's interest in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Try' and 'to' stay as written: the first holds 'everyone's' followed by the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To romance is to exaggerate or invent, and the result is an unbelievable account; the question mark flags this less usual sense.

clue.text: Pirate, before being at sea, regularly lost

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A pirate, prior to going to sea, kept getting lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the pirate scene so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeboot is to act as a freebooter, plundering as a pirate does; both work as verbs.

clue.text: A white band of cloth

blocks.note: surface reading: a plain white strip of fabric
setter's reading: 'the cloth' is the clergy, so a white band worn by its members

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of cloth' seems to name the material, but 'the cloth' is a standard term for the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests and ministers wear a stiff white neckband, the dog collar, that marks their office.

clue.text: Distant from strange person

blocks.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
an odd or queer fish is a strange person

explanation.surface: Keeping one's distance from an odd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distant from' reads as a single phrase, but 'from' supplies two letters of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish is an informal word for aloof or standoffish, someone emotionally remote.

clue.text: Iron, sulphur, copper, oriental grass

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
E for eastern, the abbreviation for oriental

explanation.surface: A chemist's list of elements found in some Asian grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Three chemical symbols then a compass letter; 'oriental' looks like a description of the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a common genus of fine-leaved pasture and lawn grasses.

clue.text: After cooking, crash out

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

blocks.note: food that is cooking is on the stove
to crash into is to strike, hit

explanation.surface: Exhausted after making dinner, someone falls asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash out' looks like slang for falling asleep, but 'out' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who are out have walked off the job in an industrial dispute.

clue.text: Being a killer contributes to panic in general

indicators.note: words that contribute to a phrase supply part of it, so the letters sit across them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A murderous streak adds to widespread panic.
explanation.walkthrough: To ice someone is American gangster slang for murder, so the act of doing it is killing.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang icing a victim means murdering them, which is what a killer does.

clue.text: One teacher turned up in place of pupil

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read bottom to top

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher arrives to cover for a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as 'instead of', but the pupil is the eye's, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured ring of the eye in whose centre the dark opening sits.

clue.text: Woven in coir, items of equal size

indicators.note: woven strands are interlaced and rearranged, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Things woven from coconut fibre all turn out the same size.
explanation.walkthrough: Coir is coconut-husk fibre used for doormats.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric means having equal dimensions or measurements throughout.

clue.text: A fighter over 9

blocks.note: taken as written
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A fighter plane flying above the clue numbered 9.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is a cross-reference: the answer to 9 across, which here means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, the slang sense of the earlier answer, a mate.

clue.text: London suburb — hotel area of course

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A is the abbreviation for area
'of course' is an emphatic yes

explanation.surface: A suburban London hotel near a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of course' suggests golf, but it splits into two separate pieces. Hayes is a district in west London near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hayes is a residential district in the borough of Hillingdon, on London's western edge.

clue.text: Focus on small vessel coming in

indicators.note: something coming in enters, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: slight means small or slender
a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: Watch out for a little boat approaching harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat coming into port, but it is a container; 'small' is not describing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spotlight something is to draw attention to it, directing attention its way as a stage lamp does.
